Write src/primerRecord/importGaps.ts, a new file. Its only import: `import { posix } from "node:path"`. Export exactly the interfaces CodeText {path: string; text: string} and LayerGap {from: string; to: string; file: string} and the function importGaps(language: string, module: string, files: readonly CodeText[], edges: Record<string, string[]>): LayerGap[]. "An own key of edges" is Object.hasOwn(edges, key).

## Function Import Gaps

The imports between code directories that the record's layer edges do not allow, one per pair of directories; pure.

Behaviour: src/primerRecord/importGaps.ts exports importGaps(language: string, module: string, files: readonly CodeText[], edges: Record<string, string[]>): LayerGap[] and the interfaces CodeText {path, text} and LayerGap {from, to, file}; it imports node:path only. edges is rules' Layer Edges result (a code directory → the directories it may import). Per file in the given order, dir = posix.dirname(path); a file whose dir is not an own key of edges is skipped. Its imported directories: typescript — every match of /\bfrom\s*["']([^"']+)["']|\bimport\s*["']([^"']+)["']/g in the text (import and export from, a side-effect import; a type import too) whose specifier starts with "./" or "../", each posix.dirname(posix.join(dir, specifier)); package and node: specifiers are no directory. go — the quoted path of each import: a line matching ^\s*import\s+(?:[\w.]+\s+)?"([^"]+)"; and, after a line matching ^\s*import\s*\(, each line matching ^\s*(?:[\w.]+\s+)?"([^"]+)" up to the first line whose trim is ")"; a path beginning module + "/" gives its rest (module "" → none). Any other language → []. A directory t gives a gap {from: dir, to: t, file: path} when t differs from dir, t is an own key of edges, and edges[dir] does not hold t; one gap per (from, to), the first file kept. The gaps sorted by from, then to (code-unit order).

Steps:
- reads: Code Text
- produces: Layer Gap

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given examples.json["Import Gaps 1"].given: typescript, four files of src/a, src/b and src/e (a type import, an export from, a side-effect import, a multi-line import, a node: import, single quotes), edges {"src/a": ["src/b"], "src/b": [], "src/c": [], "src/d": []}; when importGaps; then exactly examples.json["Import Gaps 1"].then: [{from "src/a", to "src/c", file "src/a/x.ts"}, {from "src/a", to "src/d", file "src/a/x.ts"}, {from "src/b", to "src/a", file "src/b/y.ts"}] (ref: tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json)
2. given examples.json["Import Gaps 2"].given: go, module "example.com/m", an import block with an alias and a standard package, two single-line imports of one package (one aliased), a file of cmd/ (no key of edges), edges {"internal/a": ["internal/c"], "internal/b": [], "internal/c": []}; when importGaps; then exactly examples.json["Import Gaps 2"].then: [{from "internal/a", to "internal/b", file "internal/a/a.go"}, {from "internal/b", to "internal/a", file "internal/b/b.go"}] (ref: tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json)
3. given examples.json["Import Gaps 3"].given: python with a relative import; then example 2's go files with module ""; when importGaps; then []; then [] (ref: tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json)

Data Code Text: One code file and its text (CodeText in src/primerRecord/importGaps.ts).
Schema:
{ path: string, text: string }

Data Layer Gap: An import the record's layer edges do not allow (LayerGap in src/primerRecord/importGaps.ts).
Schema:
{ from: string, to: string, file: string }

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.
- No Shell (definition not found in the record)
- No Network (definition not found in the record)
- No Env (definition not found in the record)
- No Process (definition not found in the record)

TypeScript with `strict` on, ESM with NodeNext resolution: every relative import carries the `.js` extension and types are imported with `import type`. No `any`: use `unknown` and narrow. Tests are vitest: `toBe` on scalars and short strings, `toStrictEqual` on a whole result; stubs come from `tests/helpers.ts`, never your own.

Write src/primerRecord/recordGaps.ts, a new file. Imports: `import type { ContourMap, ContourRecord } from "../contour/types.js"`, `import type { LanguageProfile } from "../language/types.js"`, resolveProfile from "../language/profiles.js", cutTargets and slugName from "../language/naming.js", codeTargets, hasExtension, isTest and normalizePath from "../language/paths.js"; nothing else. Export exactly: the interfaces NotBuilt {component: string; function: string; reason: string}, ComponentWeight {component: string; bytes: number}, RecordInputs and RecordGaps with the fields of the Data Objects Record Inputs and Record Gaps (notBuilt: NotBuilt[], weights: ComponentWeight[]), and the functions recordGaps, codeFiles and componentWeights. A map card in ContourMap is an element of map.cards (an array of {id, targets, ...}); a map group is an element of map.groups ({name, functions}). UTF-8 byte length: Buffer.byteLength(line, "utf8").

## Function Record Gaps

What the record names and the tree lacks, what the tree holds and the record does not name, the Components' weights and the record warnings; pure.

Behaviour: src/primerRecord/recordGaps.ts exports recordGaps(input: RecordInputs): RecordGaps, codeFiles(profile: LanguageProfile, files: readonly string[]): string[] and componentWeights(text: string): ComponentWeight[], and the interfaces RecordInputs, RecordGaps, NotBuilt and ComponentWeight. codeFiles: the files with language's hasExtension(profile, f) and not isTest(profile, f), whose normalizePath(f).split("/") has a first segment other than "decks", no segment beginning with "." or "_", and no directory segment (any but the last) named "vendor", "testdata" or "node_modules"; sorted in code-unit order. componentWeights: the text split on "\n", a last empty piece dropped; the first line whose trim is "groups:" opens the groups (none → []); after it, a line matching ^( *)- name:(.*)$ whose indentation equals the first such line's opens a group named by the rest trimmed (one pair of surrounding " or ' removed); a group runs until the next opening line, or until a line that is not blank, whose trim does not start with "#", and whose indentation is less than the opening indentation + 2 — such a line ends the groups (blank and comment lines inside a group belong to it); bytes = the sum over the group's lines of their UTF-8 byte length + 1. Sorted by bytes descending, then component in code-unit order. recordGaps: listed = the set of input.files. For each Component c in record order and each of its Functions f — the targets as Layer Edges finds them: profile = language's resolveProfile(c.language, map.language) (not ok → the Component's Functions are skipped); unit = the name of the map group whose functions hold f.name, else f.name; the map card whose id is slugName(unit) with targets not null gives its targets, else cutTargets(profile, c.name, unit) (not ok → skipped) gives [code, test]. Every target joins the named set. codes = codeTargets(profile, targets); missing = the codes not listed: any → notBuilt {component, function, reason "missing " + missing ", "-joined}; else when codes is not empty and none is in input.owned → reason "no Morph-Card commit". notRecorded = codeFiles(input.profile, input.files) not in the named set. weights = componentWeights(input.recordText). warnings, each text once (the first kept): input.loaderWarnings in order; then per Component in record order with language null and map.language null "no language on Component <name> and none in the map: typescript assumed"; then per Component and Function in record order, per step with verb reads, modifies or produces whose target is no Data Object or Event name of any Component "<Component>/<Function>: step <verb> '<target>' names no Data Object or Event of the record", then when f has no examples "<Component>/<Function>: no examples, no judge". components = the Components' count; functions = the count of their Functions.

Steps:
- uses: contour
- uses: language
- reads: Record Inputs
- produces: Record Gaps

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given examples.json["Record Gaps 1"].given: the fixture project repo/ — its contour.yaml loaded by loadContour (record, warnings as loaderWarnings; recordText = the text) and morph-map.json by loadMap, files and owned as listed, profile TYPESCRIPT; when recordGaps; then exactly examples.json["Record Gaps 1"].then: components 3, functions 4; notBuilt units/Format Total "missing src/units/formatTotal.ts" then units/Parse Line "no Morph-Card commit"; notRecorded ["src/index.ts", "src/units/money.ts"]; weights heavy 31358, units 1007, report 497; 5 warnings, the first "System.groups[0]: unknown key 'owner' (ignored)" (ref: tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json, tests/fixtures/primerRecord/repo/)
2. given examples.json["Record Gaps 2"].given: 13 paths, profile TYPESCRIPT; when codeFiles; then exactly examples.json["Record Gaps 2"].then: ["src/a.ts", "src/b.ts", "src/c.tsx", "src/vendor.ts"] (ref: tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json)
3. given examples.json["Record Gaps 3"].given.texts: a record text with groups a, "b" (quoted) and 'é', a blank line and a comment inside a; then a text with no "groups:" line; when componentWeights; then exactly examples.json["Record Gaps 3"].then: [{component "a", bytes 44}, {component "é", bytes 37}, {component "b", bytes 36}]; then [] (ref: tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json)

Data Record Inputs: What Record Gaps reads (TypeScript RecordInputs in src/primerRecord/recordGaps.ts).
Schema:
{ record: ContourRecord, map: ContourMap, recordText: string, loaderWarnings: string[], files: readonly string[], profile: LanguageProfile, owned: readonly string[] }

Data Record Gaps: What Record Gaps returns (RecordGaps; NotBuilt and ComponentWeight beside it in recordGaps.ts).
Schema:
{ components: number, functions: number, notBuilt: { component: string, function: string, reason: string }[], notRecorded: string[], weights: { component: string, bytes: number }[], warnings: string[] }

Write src/primerRecord/renderRecord.ts, a new file. Its only imports: `import type { RecordGaps } from "./recordGaps.js"` and `import type { LayerGap } from "./importGaps.js"` (another card writes those files: RecordGaps is {components: number; functions: number; notBuilt: {component: string; function: string; reason: string}[]; notRecorded: string[]; weights: {component: string; bytes: number}[]; warnings: string[]}, LayerGap is {from: string; to: string; file: string}). Export exactly: `export type RecordSection = { state: "not read"; reason: string } | { state: "read"; gaps: RecordGaps; layers: { checked: false; reason: string } | { checked: true; gaps: LayerGap[] } }`, `export const RECORD_CAP = 10`, `export const WEIGHT_RULE = 30000` and renderRecord. tests/fixtures/primerRecord/section1.md in your context is the exact output for a section read with every list; it begins with an empty line.

## Function Render Record

The "Record vs code" section as markdown, every list capped and its cap named; pure.

Behaviour: src/primerRecord/renderRecord.ts exports renderRecord(section: RecordSection): string, the type RecordSection, and RECORD_CAP = 10 and WEIGHT_RULE = 30000; it imports only the types RecordGaps (from ./recordGaps.js) and LayerGap (from ./importGaps.js). Lines joined "\n", the text ending "\n": "", "## Record vs code", "". state "not read" → "- record: not read: <reason>" and nothing else. state "read": "- record: read: <components> Component|Components, <functions> Function|Functions (contour.yaml, morph-map.json)" (the singular for 1). A list with a title and items: none → "- <title>: none"; else "- <title> (<n>):", then "  - <item>" for each of the first RECORD_CAP items, then "  - … +<n − RECORD_CAP> more" when n > RECORD_CAP. In order: the list "recorded, not built" of notBuilt as "<component>/<function>: <reason>"; the list "built, not recorded" of notRecorded; weights — none → "- Component weight: none", else "- Component weight, heaviest first (<k> of <n> over 30000 bytes):" (k = the weights with bytes > WEIGHT_RULE), "  - <component>: <bytes> bytes" + " — over the rule" when bytes > WEIGHT_RULE for the first RECORD_CAP, then the "… +<m> more" line as a list's; the list "record warnings" of warnings; layers checked false → "- layer gaps: not checked: <reason>", else the list "layer gaps" of the gaps as "<from> → <to> (<file>)".

Steps:
- reads: Record Section

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given examples.json["Render Record 1"].given: state "read", gaps = Record Gaps 1's result, layers checked with the gap src/units → src/report (src/units/money.ts); when renderRecord; then exactly section1.md: "- record: read: 3 Components, 4 Functions (contour.yaml, morph-map.json)", "- recorded, not built (2):", "- Component weight, heaviest first (1 of 3 over 30000 bytes):", " - heavy: 31358 bytes — over the rule", "- record warnings (5):", "- layer gaps (1):", " - src/units → src/report (src/units/money.ts)" (ref: tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json, tests/fixtures/primerRecord/section1.md)
2. given examples.json["Render Record 2"].given: 11 Components, 0 Functions, 12 paths not recorded, 11 weights 30002 down to 29992, no warnings, layers not checked "decks/tools/guard.mjs speaks contract 1"; when renderRecord; then exactly examples.json["Render Record 2"].then: "- recorded, not built: none", "- built, not recorded (12):" with src/f01.ts … src/f10.ts then " - … +2 more", "- Component weight, heaviest first (2 of 11 over 30000 bytes):" (30000 is not over), " - … +1 more", "- record warnings: none", "- layer gaps: not checked: decks/tools/guard.mjs speaks contract 1" (ref: tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json)
3. given {state "not read", reason "no contour.yaml"}; when renderRecord; then "\n## Record vs code\n\n- record: not read: no contour.yaml\n"
4. given examples.json["Render Record 4"].given: 1 Component, 1 Function, notBuilt k/F "no Morph-Card commit", no weights, warnings ["w"], layers checked with no gap; when renderRecord; then exactly examples.json["Render Record 4"].then: "- record: read: 1 Component, 1 Function (contour.yaml, morph-map.json)", "- Component weight: none", "- layer gaps: none" (ref: tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json)

Data Record Section: What Render Record renders (RecordSection in src/primerRecord/renderRecord.ts).

{ state: 'not read', reason: string } | { state: 'read', gaps: RecordGaps, layers: { checked: false, reason: string } | { checked: true, gaps: LayerGap[] } }

Write ONLY tests/primerRecord/importGaps.examples.test.ts: three tests named "Import Gaps example 1: …", "Import Gaps example 2: …", "Import Gaps example 3: …". Every expected value comes from tests/fixtures/primerRecord/examples.json, read with `const EX = fixtureJson("primerRecord/examples.json") as Record<string, { given: unknown; then: unknown }>;` and narrowed with `as` to the types named here; never `any`. ## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.
- No Shell (definition not found in the record)
- No Network (definition not found in the record)
- No Env (definition not found in the record)
- No Process (definition not found in the record)

Callee Record Gaps: What the record names and the tree lacks, what the tree holds and the record does not name, the Components' weights and the record warnings; pure.
Behaviour: src/primerRecord/recordGaps.ts exports recordGaps(input: RecordInputs): RecordGaps, codeFiles(profile: LanguageProfile, files: readonly string[]): string[] and componentWeights(text: string): ComponentWeight[], and the interfaces RecordInputs, RecordGaps, NotBuilt and ComponentWeight. codeFiles: the files with language's hasExtension(profile, f) and not isTest(profile, f), whose normalizePath(f).split("/") has a first segment other than "decks", no segment beginning with "." or "_", and no directory segment (any but the last) named "vendor", "testdata" or "node_modules"; sorted in code-unit order. componentWeights: the text split on "\n", a last empty piece dropped; the first line whose trim is "groups:" opens the groups (none → []); after it, a line matching ^( *)- name:(.*)$ whose indentation equals the first such line's opens a group named by the rest trimmed (one pair of surrounding " or ' removed); a group runs until the next opening line, or until a line that is not blank, whose trim does not start with "#", and whose indentation is less than the opening indentation + 2 — such a line ends the groups (blank and comment lines inside a group belong to it); bytes = the sum over the group's lines of their UTF-8 byte length + 1. Sorted by bytes descending, then component in code-unit order. recordGaps: listed = the set of input.files. For each Component c in record order and each of its Functions f — the targets as Layer Edges finds them: profile = language's resolveProfile(c.language, map.language) (not ok → the Component's Functions are skipped); unit = the name of the map group whose functions hold f.name, else f.name; the map card whose id is slugName(unit) with targets not null gives its targets, else cutTargets(profile, c.name, unit) (not ok → skipped) gives [code, test]. Every target joins the named set. codes = codeTargets(profile, targets); missing = the codes not listed: any → notBuilt {component, function, reason "missing " + missing ", "-joined}; else when codes is not empty and none is in input.owned → reason "no Morph-Card commit". notRecorded = codeFiles(input.profile, input.files) not in the named set. weights = componentWeights(input.recordText). warnings, each text once (the first kept): input.loaderWarnings in order; then per Component in record order with language null and map.language null "no language on Component <name> and none in the map: typescript assumed"; then per Component and Function in record order, per step with verb reads, modifies or produces whose target is no Data Object or Event name of any Component "<Component>/<Function>: step <verb> '<target>' names no Data Object or Event of the record", then when f has no examples "<Component>/<Function>: no examples, no judge". components = the Components' count; functions = the count of their Functions.

Callee Import Gaps: The imports between code directories that the record's layer edges do not allow, one per pair of directories; pure.
Behaviour: src/primerRecord/importGaps.ts exports importGaps(language: string, module: string, files: readonly CodeText[], edges: Record<string, string[]>): LayerGap[] and the interfaces CodeText {path, text} and LayerGap {from, to, file}; it imports node:path only. edges is rules' Layer Edges result (a code directory → the directories it may import). Per file in the given order, dir = posix.dirname(path); a file whose dir is not an own key of edges is skipped. Its imported directories: typescript — every match of /\bfrom\s*["']([^"']+)["']|\bimport\s*["']([^"']+)["']/g in the text (import and export from, a side-effect import; a type import too) whose specifier starts with "./" or "../", each posix.dirname(posix.join(dir, specifier)); package and node: specifiers are no directory. go — the quoted path of each import: a line matching ^\s*import\s+(?:[\w.]+\s+)?"([^"]+)"; and, after a line matching ^\s*import\s*\(, each line matching ^\s*(?:[\w.]+\s+)?"([^"]+)" up to the first line whose trim is ")"; a path beginning module + "/" gives its rest (module "" → none). Any other language → []. A directory t gives a gap {from: dir, to: t, file: path} when t differs from dir, t is an own key of edges, and edges[dir] does not hold t; one gap per (from, to), the first file kept. The gaps sorted by from, then to (code-unit order).

Callee Render Record: The "Record vs code" section as markdown, every list capped and its cap named; pure.
Behaviour: src/primerRecord/renderRecord.ts exports renderRecord(section: RecordSection): string, the type RecordSection, and RECORD_CAP = 10 and WEIGHT_RULE = 30000; it imports only the types RecordGaps (from ./recordGaps.js) and LayerGap (from ./importGaps.js). Lines joined "\n", the text ending "\n": "", "## Record vs code", "". state "not read" → "- record: not read: <reason>" and nothing else. state "read": "- record: read: <components> Component|Components, <functions> Function|Functions (contour.yaml, morph-map.json)" (the singular for 1). A list with a title and items: none → "- <title>: none"; else "- <title> (<n>):", then "  - <item>" for each of the first RECORD_CAP items, then "  - … +<n − RECORD_CAP> more" when n > RECORD_CAP.
